role: Bus-routing specialist: actual CONTROL_I2C trunks and SDA/SCL branches

directChecks.evidence: source_bus_0 CONTROL_I2C contains source_trace_1024 and source_trace_1025; actual pcb_trace_542 and pcb_trace_543 own the corresponding two source traces.
SCL source_net_59 connectivity_net4; SDA source_net_60 connectivity_net5. All 16 actual copper paths resolve to their intended net through source_trace connectivity keys.

Exhaustive nonzero same-layer line-segment pairs against all PCB traces using segment intersection / minimum endpoint-to-segment distance, then subtracting half trace widths. Global bus-scope minimum foreign copper-edge trace gap 0.2631549416771887 mm.
Exhaustive I2C segment-to-via comparisons on shared layers, with via outer copper diameter and wire halfwidth subtracted. Minimum gap 0.20000000000000015 mm.
I2C_MCU_DAC_SCL / I2C_MCU_DAC_SDA are 0.20 mm wide, top only, with no layer changes and at least 0.75 mm edge spacing.
Six named 0.30/0.70 mm full-stack vias: one launch for each net at DAC, PD, monitor. Long PD branches remain bottom; long monitor branches remain inner2. No intermediate meandering layer swaps.
TP10_I2C_TAP and TP11_I2C_TAP are each 1.50 mm actual top copper and meet same-net vertical DAC trunk at (0, -16.5) and (0.95, -16.5).

strengths: The two real main bus trunks are short, simple, ordered and entirely on top; 6.8659 mm SCL and 6.4724 mm SDA, each approximately 1.08 times the straight pad-to-pad distance.
The branches use deliberate source-owned layer assignments and six common launch barrels; there is no repeated midspan bouncing between layers.
The monitor branches are close to an octilinear minimum: 49.2068 and 49.3657 mm, only 1.062 and 1.061 times their straight-line distances.
Debug test points create short deliberate 1.5 mm stubs, avoiding long side excursions.
This review did not find a same-layer foreign-net overlap in the actual I2C trace/via geometry.

findings.explanation: The beautiful declared CONTROL_I2C bus is only the short MCU-to-DAC trunk. The longer inner2 monitor branches use nonuniform pairing; their closest SCL/SDA copper-edge spacing is 0.263155 mm. This does not violate the top-only bus setting, but the visual consistency and routing margin could be improved by routing the whole monitor branch as an intentional pair.

The long SDA vertical branch passes a full-stack HOT_ADC via at exactly 0.20 mm copper-edge margin on both bottom and inner2. There is no overlap, but this is a denser and less forgiving bus corridor than the main top bus.

The SDA pullup connection walks 6.1627 mm while the SCL pullup link is 0.8828 mm. This is not a blocking electrical issue for the intended low-speed bus, but moving the pullup beside the PD SDA launch would improve local organization and shorten the pullup branch. Electrical speed or RC compliance was not established here.

suspectedShortAssessment.result: No foreign-net overlap found among the I2C traces and shared-layer vias. The image crop alone is not enough to identify ownership/layer; its particular location was not identified by this role, so no board-wide short claim is made.

topImprovements: Extend deliberate bus pairing to the long monitor branches with a more consistent gap, while preserving existing foreign-net clearances.
Give the SDA corridor additional room around HOT_ADC / VOUT_ADC launch barrels if placement permits.
Place PD pullups together at their SDA/SCL launch vias to avoid the asymmetric 6.16 mm SDA pullup excursion.
limitations: This role checks bus routing, not the full board.
The exhaustive clearance checks include traces and vias, but do not independently expand pads, polygons/pours, or fabrication mask geometries.
No bus pullup capacitance, rise time, operating speed, switching-noise waveform, manufacturing or bench readiness claim is made.
101.8154 mm SCL / 109.3358 mm SDA totals are sums of route records and include same-net shared/overlapping top copper; they are not unique conductor lengths.
